resolution: event/abbasid-investiture-ibn-hud, dated 1228~ (AH 626~), is placed in the contested reign of the Almohad Yahya ibn al-Nasir, and that placing is right. The wrong side is the caliph's death date, not the event. person/al-muhtadid-yahya-almohad carries died 1224~ (AH 621~), but the only source it cites for his death, Wafayat al-A'yan (Ihsan Abbas edition, vol. 7 pp. 16-17, read in the harvest copy), gives no year for it: it tells his killing near Tlemcen after Ibn Hud's rising and after Idris al-Ma'mun took Marrakesh, which the museum's own records put in 626 AH, and the record's own story_role has him ruling 1227-1229. So 621 cannot be his death year, and no source the record cites supplies the right one (the Bayan al-Mughrib named on its relations has no passage on him in the harvest copy). It stands until a source that dates his death is added: proposed replacement, or removal, of `died` in data/person/al-muhtadid-yahya-almohad.yaml, which is the founder's decision.

The relation pointed at the wrong caliph. person/abd-al-wahid-ii-almohad's own summary and prose are about Abd al-Wahid ibn Yusuf, strangled in Sha'ban 621 AH (1224) after nine months ({cite:shadharat-dhahab p. 96}); he cannot be the Almohad caliph of 1266-1269. That caliph, the successor of al-Murtada, is al-Wathiq Abu Dabbus, who has the record person/al-wathiq-abu-dabus (took Marrakesh in Muharram 665 AH, ruled three years, killed in Muharram 668 AH: {cite:wafayat-ayan p. 15-16} as that record cites it, read on p. 18 of vol. 7 in the harvest copy). Retargeted during_reign in data/event/battle-of-telagh-1268.yaml from person/abd-al-wahid-ii-almohad to person/al-wathiq-abu-dabus; nothing else in the file was touched. The event card itself names no ruler, so the support is in the two person records' own cited sources (Shadharat al-Dhahab p. 96 for the man who died in 621 AH; Wafayat al-A'yan pp. 15-16 for the caliph of 665-668 AH), not in a source the event cites. The battle is dated 1268, inside Abu Dabbus's reign. Left for the founder: person/abd-al-wahid-ii-almohad still carries the 1266-1269 story_role and the successor_of al-Murtada relation that belong to Abu Dabbus; moving them means removing them from that record.

The child_of relation to person/khadija is right; the wrong side is the child's dates. person/al-qasim-ibn-muhammad is the Prophet's son by Khadija, who by the record's own prose was born in Mecca before the prophethood and died in infancy ({cite:mubarakpuri-raheeq p. 473}; {cite:zad-al-maad}). Its born 1559 and died 1620 were written by the date-enrichment pass (note: al-A'lam) and are evidently those of a later man of the same name. None of the record's cited sources gives a year for his birth or death, so there is nothing to put in their place: proposed removal of `born` and `died` from data/person/al-qasim-ibn-muhammad.yaml, the founder's decision. The Arabic summary of the same record also carries two sentences about another namesake (died 108 AH, one of the jurists consulted by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz), which need the same decision.

The dates agree with each other; the predicate is what is wrong. event/death-of-habib-ibn-maslama (42 AH) retells al-Baladhuri's whole passage, in which Uthman gave the Armenian frontier to Hudhayfa after Habib, years before Habib died ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 287-288}); Hudhayfa died in 36 AH and took no part in the death. The event's own file already records the link correctly as related_to person/hudhayfa-ibn-al-yaman with the same role, so the person-side relation is a second, stronger writing of the same edge. Fixing it means removing a relation, which is the founder's decision: proposed removal of `participated_in -> event/death-of-habib-ibn-maslama` from data/person/hudhayfa-ibn-al-yaman.yaml.

The person's death date was wrong: died 750~ came from the date-enrichment pass (note: al-Tabari, no page), while the record's own prose and cited source say al-Mansur had him killed at al-Raqqa in the year 141 AH ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 271}, checked in the harvest copy). Corrected `died` in data/person/mansur-ibn-jamwana.yaml from edtf 750~ to edtf 0758~ with hijri 0141, the same pair the event of his killing already carries (no new conversion), and cited the record's own source on the date.

The wrong side is the death date. person/sarjun-ibn-mansur carries died 690~ (and born 660~), estimates from the date-enrichment pass (note: al-Tabari, no page). The record's own cited source has Abd al-Malik summon Sarjun to see the finished transfer of the diwan, which was ordered in 81 AH (700) ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 271-272}, checked in the harvest copy), so he was alive after 690; neither that source nor the Fihrist gives his death year. Nothing cited can replace the date: proposed removal of `died` from data/person/sarjun-ibn-mansur.yaml, the founder's decision (born 660~ needs the same look: the record says he already kept the diwan for Mu'awiya).

The wrong side is the death date. person/umm-muni-asma-bint-amr carries died 622~, an estimate from the date-enrichment pass (its own note reads '~640', a different year). The record's cited source says, from Ibn Sa'd, that she witnessed Khaybar in 7 AH ({cite:nisa-hawl-alrasul p. 274}), and the record's own prose states that no birth or death date was written because the source had not been read. Al-Isaba, also cited by the record, gives no death year in her entry (harvest copy, entries 10852 and 12319). Nothing cited can replace the date: proposed removal of `died` from data/person/umm-muni-asma-bint-amr.yaml, the founder's decision.

event/conquest-of-kamkh is one record for several takings of the fortress and is dated by the first, 59 AH (678); its own summary and date note go on to the sieges of 149 AH, 177 AH and al-Ma'mun's caliphate ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 259-261}). Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad's relation carries the role 'commander of the siege of the year 149' (766), when a man born in 738 was about twenty-eight. The detector compared his birth with the event's first episode only; the two records agree.

The dates are right on both sides (al-Mada'ini 752-843; the papyrus affair under Abd al-Malik, about 692); the predicate is what is wrong. Al-Mada'ini is the narrator of one report of the affair, as the relation's own role ('narrator of the embargo report'), the person's prose and the cited source say ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 335-336}); he did not take part in it. The event's own file already records him correctly as related_to with the same role, so the person-side relation is a second, stronger writing of the same edge. Fixing it means removing a relation, which is the founder's decision: proposed removal of `participated_in -> event/qaratis-dinar-crisis` from data/person/al-madaini.yaml.

The year was keyed under the wrong life event. person/dhu-al-khuwaysira carried born 658~ (date-enrichment pass, note: Fath al-Bari), impossible for a man who confronted the Prophet at al-Ji'rana in 8 AH (630). The record's own prose says he later became a Kharijite leader and was killed at al-Nahrawan ({cite:ibn-hisham-saqqa 4/140}), and the museum's event/battle-of-nahrawan is dated 38 AH, which is 658: the year is his death, not his birth. Changed the field name from `born` to `died` in data/person/dhu-al-khuwaysira.yaml, leaving the value 658~ and its note as they were. One caution for the re-check: the harvest holds a different edition of Ibn Hisham, so the Saqqa page for the death at al-Nahrawan was taken from the record's prose and not re-read.

The wrong side is the person's dates. person/mushayil-al-armani carries born 900~ and died 930~, estimates from the date-enrichment pass (note: al-Tabari, no page), while its own cited source says he led the Armenian rising in al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba's governorship and was killed when al-Mansur sent reinforcements, that is within al-Mansur's caliphate, 754-775 ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 295}). The source gives no birth year, so the finding cannot be removed without deleting `born`: proposed removal of `born` from data/person/mushayil-al-armani.yaml and replacement of `died` by the event's own range 0754/0775, the founder's decision.

Two things meet here. event/treaty-with-jarajima is dated by the first treaty (about 16 AH, 637) but its summary runs on to the days of Ibn al-Zubayr, when Abd al-Malik sent Suhaym against the Byzantine commander ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 217-219}); Suhaym belongs to that later episode, so the event's date is not the problem. The problem is his own dates: born 680~ and died 700~ are estimates from the date-enrichment pass (note: al-Tabari, no page), and a man sent on that mission in Ibn al-Zubayr's days (ended 73 AH, 692) cannot have been born about 680. The cited source gives no birth or death year, so nothing can replace them: proposed removal of `born` and `died` from data/person/suhaym-ibn-al-muhajir.yaml, the founder's decision.

The relation was written backwards: person/nusayr-father-of-musa was child_of person/musa-ibn-nusayr, though the record's own label, summary and cited source make Nusayr the father ('Musa was born to him at the village of Kafr Mari', {cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 345-346}, checked in the harvest copy). Changed the relation type from child_of to parent_of in data/person/nusayr-father-of-musa.yaml; Musa's file does not write the edge, so it is now written once and in the right direction. Still standing, for the founder: Nusayr's born 633~ is a date-enrichment value and is the year of his capture at Ayn al-Tamr in the record's own account, not a birth year; it leaves the father seven years older than the son (born 640~).

The student_of relation is right; the wrong side is the student's dates. person/ahmad-ibn-yahya-al-mutakallim carries born 850~ and died 900~ from the date-enrichment pass (note: Ibn al-Nadim, al-Fihrist), evidently a later namesake's, while its only cited source calls him one of the senior companions of al-Shafi'i (died 820) who then joined Ibn Abi Du'ad ({cite:tabaqat-fuqaha-abbas-1981 p. 54}); the record's own summary says al-Shirazi gives no death date and its prose says the birth date needs another source. Nothing cited can replace the dates: proposed removal of `born` and `died` from data/person/ahmad-ibn-yahya-al-mutakallim.yaml, the founder's decision.

One of the two relations is backwards. data/person/muhammad-ibn-sirin.yaml rightly writes child_of person/sirin-father-of-ibn-sirin; data/person/sirin-father-of-ibn-sirin.yaml wrongly writes child_of person/muhammad-ibn-sirin, though its own label, summary and prose make Sirin the father ({cite:futuh-buldan-maarif-1407 p. 345-347}). Turning the wrong one into parent_of would only write the same edge a second time from the other side, which the museum's rule (each edge once) and the relation check refuse; the real fix is to take it out, and a removal is the founder's decision: proposed removal of `child_of -> person/muhammad-ibn-sirin` from data/person/sirin-father-of-ibn-sirin.yaml.

The parenthesis gives al-Mahdi's caliphate, not his life: the sentence says the siqaya was built 'under the Abbasid caliph al-Mahdi (158-169 AH)', in Arabic 'in the caliphate of al-Mahdi'. person/al-mahdi records a rule of 775-785 and a death in 169 AH after a caliphate of ten years, which is the same span. The two records agree.
